data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'wursa', meaning 'bear cub' or 'bear son'. The name Orson has historical roots in the Anglo-Saxon culture, and its popularity can be attributed to its strong and powerful meaning. The name Orson carries the meaning “Little bear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Orson usually hope their child will grow to embody little bear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Orson belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little bear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Orson total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: אורסון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew words ‘aur’ (mountain, strength) and ‘son’ (man). It means ‘strong, bear, mighty man’.

in_greek.name: Ορσον
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word ‘oros’ (mountain) and ‘son’ (man). It means ‘mountain man’.

in_latin.name: Orsonius
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word ‘orsus’ (mountain) and ‘ius’ (man). It means ‘mountain man’.

in_english.name: Orson
in_english.long_meaning: From the Old English words ‘weor’ (man) and ‘sige’ (victory, power). It means ‘bear, man, victorious one’.

data.cultural_impact: Orson is a name with historical roots in Anglo-Saxon culture, derived from the Old English word 'wursa', meaning 'bear cub' or 'bear son'. Its strong and powerful meaning has made it a popular name among Christians, representing courage, strength, and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Orson holds a deep symbolism of the bear as a powerful and protective figure. In the Bible, the Prophet Hosea compares God to a bear, saying, "I will entice them with wild asses' colts, with young donkeys, I will give them their calves' faces - with this I will soothe their despair." (Hosea 11:10). The name Orson, symbolizing a bear cub or bear son, can be seen as a reminder of the protective and nurturing nature of God. It also holds a connection to the spiritual belief in the power of Christianity to protect and strengthen individuals, just as a bear mother protects and nurtures her cubs.
